title: Ongoing
description: Which local projects deserve attention: one API, two clients, a cache-first scanner, and an app-owned catalog.
provenance: Authored 2026-09-11 from the Ongoing source tree, ADRs, README, AGENTS.md, deployment and website docs; updated 2026-09-11 when Phase 1 of the inventory redesign landed. Every current component cites the files inspected. The catalog repository is modeled as one component rather than per table; the Svelte component tree and the test suites are intentionally shallow. Inside the 'Software inventory' subsystem the entries store, the field registry, the entries API, and the entry CLI verbs are now current and cite code; the query grammar, provider manifests, host adapter, deployment profiles, and the new shell stay proposed, as does the whole 'Tech radar' subsystem, and their evidence paths are plans and ADRs rather than code.

boundaries.title: Same HTTP contract
boundaries.description: Both clients go through the JSON API. A capability reachable only through the browser would be a design bug. The entries API extends the same contract to fields, relations, and saved views, and every CLI verb over them is the same route the browser calls.

boundaries.title: LAN request boundary
boundaries.description: Every request crosses the production edge and the SvelteKit gate: bounded bodies, security headers, and, when enabled, session and same-origin checks. Auth is intentionally off in production.

boundaries.title: Pure rules, no I/O
boundaries.description: Functions of normalized data only. The browser re-runs attention classification after an optimistic edit, and will validate a patch and parse a query with the same code the server runs.

boundaries.title: One scan at a time
boundaries.description: Two processes open the same SQLite file. The durable scan lease in scan_runs, heartbeated every 10 seconds, keeps a manual scan from overlapping the calendar job.

boundaries.title: Subprocess and network egress
boundaries.description: Everything that spawns a tool or leaves the machine. Each path has a timeout and an availability state; none can fail a whole scan.

boundaries.title: App-owned durable state
boundaries.description: Ongoing's SQLite file and the release tooling that backs it up, migrates it, and restores it. Never a repository's .todos database.

boundaries.title: Public website copy
boundaries.description: The only data that leaves the private dashboard: explicitly included website records, exported deterministically, without notes, paths, or scanned metrics.

boundaries.title: Proposed: switchable seams
boundaries.description: Every assumption that is currently baked in — where repositories live, who hosts them, who tracks issues, who counts lines, what runs the service, where it deploys — declared in a manifest or an adapter and switchable in one TOML file. This is what lets Ongoing run on a machine that is not aerie.

scenes.title: Ongoing at a glance
scenes.description: One local process serves a browser and a CLI from an app-owned catalog that a bounded scanner keeps fresh.

scenes.title: One API, two clients
scenes.description: The CLI and the browser are peers: both read page models and send mutations through the same routes, behind the same gate.

scenes.title: How a scan refreshes the catalog
scenes.description: Discovery first, then git, TD, and stack per project, cloc only when the worktree changed, then release baselines and GitHub once per run.

scenes.title: From cached rows to attention views
scenes.description: The read model joins catalog tables, resolves stacks against baselines, and asks the pure domain rules which views each project belongs to and why.

scenes.title: Entries, fields, and relations
scenes.description: What Phases 1 and 2 built: one entries table with a source per provider, a registry that validates every patch, one query grammar that reads them all, and one API and CLI over the lot. The project dashboard is a projection of the same rows.

scenes.title: Tools, APIs, and hosts
scenes.description: What Ongoing spawns, calls, or is scheduled by, and how each dependency is allowed to fail.

scenes.title: Running on aerie.local
scenes.description: Two launchd agents, one pinned Bun, a health-gated deploy that quiesces both before touching the database.

scenes.title: Boundaries and authority
scenes.description: Where requests are gated, which code is pure, who may hold the scan lease, what leaves the machine, and what is allowed to go public.

scenes.title: Proposal: Ongoing as a software inventory
scenes.description: Phases 1 and 2 have landed: entries, the field registry, the query grammar, the entries API, and the CLI over them are current inside this subsystem. What is still drawn as proposed is the rest of the settled design — collectors declared as providers behind a host adapter, and a keyboard-first shell that builds the same query string the CLI does.

scenes.title: The tech radar
scenes.description: Technologies as a second entry kind with rings, uses relations detected by the tech-signatures provider inside the stack collector pass or declared by hand, ongoing tech verbs over the same query model, and the generator that renders the project-standards tables. Only the radar page is still a proposal.

scenes.title: Proposal: seams and boundaries
scenes.description: The same proposed subsystem under the trust lens: which parts share the one HTTP contract, which are pure rules the browser re-runs, what the durable state is, and which pieces exist so that discovery, hosting, issues, the serving host, and the deploy target stop being assumptions.
